title: Repeating Patterns: What Comes Next and the Core
seo_title: Kindergarten Repeating patterns Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Repeating patterns with two or three elements: sorting and classifying using a single attribute, identifying patterns in the world, repeating patterns with 2-3 elements, identifying the core
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on repeating patterns for the BC curriculum: AB, AAB, ABB and ABC patterns, the core, missing pieces, sound and action patterns, and sorting by one attribute. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: The core is the part of a pattern that repeats.
key_sub: Say the pattern out loud. Find where it starts again to see the core.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A repeating pattern has a part that repeats again and again. This part is called the core.
  • Say the pattern out loud: red, blue, red, blue … Then say what comes next.
  • Patterns can have 2 or 3 things in the core: AB, AAB, ABB or ABC.
  • To sort, choose one rule, like colour or shape, and put things that match together.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Repeating the last thingSay the whole pattern out loud from the start.
Taking only one thing as the coreFind where the pattern starts again.
Sorting by colour and shape at onceChoose one rule at a time.

faq.a: A pattern where the same group of things, the core, repeats again and again, such as red, blue, red, blue.

faq.q: What is the core of a pattern?
faq.a: The shortest part that repeats. In clap, clap, stamp, clap, clap, stamp, the core is clap, clap, stamp.

faq.q: What patterns do Kindergarten children learn?
faq.a: Repeating patterns with two or three elements, such as AB, AAB, ABB and ABC, shown with objects, colours, sounds and actions.

faq.q: How does sorting help with patterns?
faq.a: Sorting by one attribute, like colour or shape, helps children notice what is the same and what changes in a pattern.

items.q: Which pattern is made the same way as red, blue, red, blue, red, blue?

green, yellow, green, yellow, green, yellow
red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue
dog, dog, cat, dog, dog, cat
